mustFix.title: The draft misstates the register status of the very row it records against: DR-122 is PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW in file 08, not OPEN

measurement.whatTheRegisterSays: File 08 line 304 is the DR-122 row. I split it on the column delimiter and read the status cell directly: it is PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW. Not OPEN.
measurement.theTokensAreDistinct: The register treats these as different states and counts them separately. The condition-2 snapshot at line 403 reads '22 OPEN, 2 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, 2 PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW', and I confirmed exactly two rows carry that third token — DR-107 at line 289 and DR-122 at line 304. So this is not a synonym or a loose paraphrase; it names the wrong member of a closed taxonomy.
measurement.theHouseConventionIsToNameTheActualToken: I checked all five sibling recordings of the same form. D-110 says 'DR-125 stays OPEN', D-111 'DR-127 stays OPEN', D-112 'DR-108 stays OPEN' — and each of those rows is genuinely OPEN. Decisively, D-113 says 'DR-118 stays DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED', and DR-118's row carries exactly that token. The convention plainly handles non-OPEN statuses correctly, so this is an outlier error and not a house shorthand.
measurement.howItLooksLikeItHappened: The phrase 'leftover-design / OPEN' is verbatim D-114's sentence about DR-101, the immediately preceding decision. 'leftover-design' occurs exactly once in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md — there — and zero times in file 08. The status clause appears to have been carried across from the predecessor decision to a different row with a different status.
measurement.whatIsAtStake: If adopted as drafted, COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md would assert a DR-122 status that file 08 contradicts, in the entry whose function is to record a candidate against that row. 'OPEN' also appears exactly once in the whole draft, so the defect is confined to this one sentence.

mustFix.whyMustFixAndNotShouldFix: It is a false statement about register state, made in the operative Decision section rather than in commentary, about the single row the decision exists to act on. The regime's whole discipline is that a recorded decision and the register agree; a coordinator entry that contradicts file 08 on the subject row is the defect that has to be corrected before adoption rather than carried as honesty work. I note the error runs in the conservative direction — OPEN claims less closure than PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW — which is why it is a correctness failure rather than an overreach, but the direction does not make the statement true.
mustFix.minimumRepair: Change item 2 to state the row's actual token: 'DR-122 stays PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW', following the form D-113 used for its non-OPEN row. Either drop 'leftover-design' or justify it for this row — it has no basis in file 08, which never uses the phrase, and its only COORD occurrence is D-114's sentence about DR-101. Nothing else in the draft needs to move: items 1 and 3 through 5, the alternatives, the readiness effect and the reversibility all stand.

verdictStatement: The draft is careful and almost everything in it holds. All five measured digests match live, including both verdict files at 0444; the 0/0 gate it rests on is real on both lanes, which I confirmed by opening the frozen verdicts rather than trusting the summary; both advisories are recorded and correctly characterised as honesty work; the register is the right file 08 and the decoy is named and avoided; D-115 is distinguished from DR-115 and D-114 from DR-114, and the subtler D-108-versus-DR-108 distinction is drawn correctly too; every row named in the disclaimer list exists; the sixteen cited precedents all exist and are the same class; and the readiness-effect claim matches the live condition-2 cell verbatim. Every one of the dispatch's twelve named attacks fails. One thing does not hold, and it is in the operative Decision section about the only row this decision concerns. Item 2 says 'DR-122 stays leftover-design / OPEN'. File 08 line 304 records DR-122 as PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, which the register treats as a distinct state — the condition-2 snapshot counts OPEN, DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED and PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW separately, and exactly two rows carry the third token. This is not house shorthand: D-113 states 'DR-118 stays DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED' for its non-OPEN row, so the convention handles these correctly. The phrase 'leftover-design / OPEN' is verbatim D-114's sentence about DR-101, and 'leftover-design' occurs once in COORD — there — and never in file 08, so the status clause appears to have been carried across from the predecessor decision to a row in a different state. Adopted as drafted, the entry would assert a DR-122 status that the register contradicts. 'OPEN' appears exactly once in the whole draft, so one sentence carries the fix.

coordinatorNote: OBJECT at turn 1 on a single sentence. The recording itself is well founded — both lanes accepted v15 at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, every digest in the table is live-accurate, and the decision correctly refuses SATISFIED, QUALIFIED, implementation authorization, a D-096 (A) grant, DR-117 disposal and any DR-103 satisfaction. I would expect a turn-2 draft to reach CONSENT on my lane with one edit: state DR-122's actual register token, PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, in item 2, in the form D-113 already used for its non-OPEN row, and drop or justify 'leftover-design' for this row since the phrase has no basis in file 08 and its only COORD occurrence is D-114's sentence about a different row. Two notes for the turn-2 author. First, the likely mechanism is a carried clause from the immediately preceding decision, so it is worth checking whether any other sentence in the draft was inherited from D-114 rather than measured for DR-122 — I found none, but I was looking for the error only after I had it. Second, my one advisory is that item 5 lists DR-115 among rows this decision does not SATISFY while the preamble correctly states DR-115 is already SATISFIED at D-089; both sentences are true under the natural reading, so I have not made it a SHOULD-FIX, but it is the only other place where two statements in this draft could be read against each other. Nothing in this verdict marks any DR SATISFIED, authorizes implementation, or mints a D-096 (A) grant, and I edited neither file 08 nor COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md.
